title: Cypherpunk Manifesto as an LP2 running key
question: Does any contiguous offset of Eric Hughes's manifesto, converted by either of two fixed key mappings and subtracted modulo 29, produce a convincing complete LP2 page?
summary: Both planted controls rank first; on each of three LP2 pages, several of sixteen equally searched shuffled keys match or beat the best manifesto score under either mapping.

scope.representation: Pinned 1993 manifesto page fetched 2026-10-23; 4,072 normalized ASCII letters from the essay body. Separate A=0..25 and greedy GP-rune key sequences; canonical 29-index ciphertext and Latin labels.
scope.procedure: At every no-wrap contiguous offset that covers the complete target page, subtract one key unit per rune modulo 29. Rank full-page English quadgram scores. Repeat the entire offset search on sixteen seeded value-shuffled keys per mapping/page. Plant an LP1-04 known reading with each mapping at offset 3301 and require rank one before LP2 scoring.
scope.parameters: Two named source mappings; LP2-00 (262 runes), LP2-31 (269), LP2-54 (232); 3,804–3,841 A–Z offsets and 3,625–3,662 GP offsets per page; 16 complete shuffled-key searches for every mapping/page; one fixed subtraction direction and scorer.
scope.exclusions: Other source editions or passages, preserving source word boundaries during GP parsing, reverse arithmetic, skip/feedback clocks, wraps, other LP2 pages, arbitrary internal starts, non-English scoring and any general rejection of running keys.

finding: For the A–Z mapping, respectively 13, 16 and 13 of 16 full-search shuffled maxima equalled or exceeded the source maximum on LP2-00, 31 and 54; for greedy GP mapping, 11, 14 and 9 of 16 did. Both positive-control searches rank the planted offset first and recover the complete LP1-04 reading.
limitations: The text is a pinned public copy, not an authenticated puzzle key. Sixteen shuffles are a coarse matched search reference and not a calibrated p-value; shuffled keys are unlike other coherent source texts. English quadgram scoring can miss meaningful non-English or nonstandard plaintext. Human review pending.
next_steps: A follow-up needs to predeclare a different source edition, encoding, cipher direction or key clock, then repeat positive controls and complete-offset null searches over entire pages.

visuals.caption: Best complete-page scores for two manifesto key mappings compared with the ranges from sixteen equally searched shuffled keys on each LP2 target.

reader_finding: The manifesto did not stand out from shuffled keys on the three tested pages. Every best-score result was matched or beaten by several shuffled-key searches.
reader_limit: Only LP2-00, 31 and 54 were tested, at every fitting offset under two fixed mappings and uninterrupted subtraction. English scoring and the preserved source edition limit the result.
